name: jupiterfetch
description: Look up a company's brand profile from its domain: logos, colors labeled by role, fonts, images and social links.

interface.longDescription:
JupiterFetch reads a company's website and returns its brand profile: logos, colors labeled by role, fonts, images and social links, from just a domain.

With JupiterFetch connected to your account, ChatGPT can:

- Look up any company's brand by its domain, or by a URL on its site.
- Give you the logo as an image link, with an SVG when the company publishes one.
- Name the primary, secondary, accent and background colors as hex values.
- Name the fonts the site uses for headings and body text.
- Tell you how many JupiterFetch credits your account has left.

Use it to build a deck or proposal in a prospect's colors, mock up a page with a client's real logo and fonts, or fill a list of companies with each one's logo and brand color.

Each answer comes from a read of the company's public website. Logo and image links are hosted on cdn.jupiterfetch.com for at least 30 days.

Each successful lookup uses one credit from your JupiterFetch account, including results served from cache. Credits are managed on jupiterfetch.com, never inside ChatGPT. Checking your balance uses none.

Limits: it reads public websites only, never pages behind a login. Some sites block automated reads; then it returns what it could get, or says why it could not, and uses no credit.

Get the logo and colors for notion.so and suggest a slide style that matches.
How many JupiterFetch credits do I have left?

positive.description: Brand colors for a company named by domain
positive.prompt: Using JupiterFetch, what are stripe.com's brand colors?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_brand with domain stripe.com. Answers with hex colors and their roles: primary #533afd, secondary #64748d, accent #00d66f. The tool's text result ends with '1 credit used, N left.'

positive.description: A logo as an image link, with its SVG
positive.prompt: Give me the logo for linear.app.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_brand with domain linear.app. Returns a https://cdn.jupiterfetch.com/linear.app/... PNG link and a vector link ending in .svg; both open in a browser.
Calls get_brand with domain linear.app (or reuses the profile from the previous turn). Names Inter Variable for body text and Berkeley Mono for code.

positive.description: A full URL is reduced to its domain
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_brand; the URL is normalized to the domain stripe.com and the Stripe profile is returned: the name Stripe, a logo link and the colors above.

positive.prompt: How many JupiterFetch credits do I have left?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_credits only (no get_brand). Reports the balance and whether auto top-up is on. Checking the balance uses no credit.

negative.description: A domain that does not exist. get_brand returns an error saying the domain does not resolve; no credit is used and no profile is invented.
A private network address. get_brand refuses it as a private address; nothing is fetched and no credit is used.
negative.prompt: Get the brand profile for http://192.168.1.1.

negative.description: A request unrelated to brands. No JupiterFetch tool is called.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in Sydney today?

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell anything or process payments. A lookup uses credits from the user's JupiterFetch account; credits are bought on jupiterfetch.com, never inside ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: First release: get_brand returns a company's brand profile (logos, colors with roles, fonts, images, social links) from its domain, and get_credits shows the account's credit balance.
